controls.name: Physical access to servers is restricted and logged
controls.objective: Prevent unauthorised physical access to server hardware, consoles and storage.
controls.business_justification: Physical access bypasses most logical controls and can lead to data theft, tampering or prolonged outage.
controls.threat: Hardware tampering, console and boot-media attacks, drive theft, rogue device insertion.
controls.assessment_question: Are servers housed in locked racks or access-controlled rooms, with access limited to authorised staff and logged?
evidence_required: colocation contract and assurance report if hosted
controls.validation_procedure:
1. Interview the facilities owner and obtain the authorised-access list.
2. Walk the server room: check rack locks, door controls, cameras and visitor escort practice.
3. Sample 10 names on the list against HR leavers and job roles; review badge logs for after-hours entry.
4. For hosted or colocation sites, obtain the provider SOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001 certificate and confirm physical controls are in scope.

automation.method: Badge-system export compared with the HR leaver list (CSV reconciliation).

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Servers sit in open or shared areas; access is ad hoc and unlogged.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Locked room or racks, documented access list, logs retained and reviewed annually.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Multi-factor physical entry, CCTV with retention, quarterly access recertification, automated leaver revocation and anomaly alerts.

controls.remediation_guidance: Move servers into locked racks or rooms, define the authorised list, enable badge logging and CCTV, and recertify access at least quarterly for sensitive sites.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 PE family; ISO/IEC 27002:2022 clause 7; NIST SP 800-88 Rev.1 (media sanitization); vendor hardware hardening guides

controls.name: Out-of-band management interfaces are isolated and hardened
controls.objective: Ensure BMC, iDRAC, iLO, IPMI and KVM-over-IP interfaces cannot be used to take over servers.
controls.business_justification: A compromised BMC gives console, power and virtual-media control that sits below the operating system and its security tooling.
controls.threat: BMC firmware and IPMI protocol exploitation, default credentials, firmware implants, remote console takeover.
controls.assessment_question: Are out-of-band management interfaces on a dedicated management network, patched, with default credentials changed and strong authentication enforced?
evidence_required: firewall rules for the management VLAN
BMC user list and authentication settings
controls.validation_procedure:
From an authorised host on the management VLAN, discover IPMI exposure with `nmap -sU -p 623 --script ipmi-version <mgmt-subnet>` and confirm IPMI-over-LAN is disabled or restricted.
Review BMC accounts, TLS certificate and firmware date in the web console or via Redfish (`curl -k -u <user> https://<bmc>/redfish/v1/Managers`).
Confirm the BMC subnet is unreachable from user and internet segments (`nc -vz <bmc-ip> 443` from a user VLAN should fail).

automation.method: Redfish API inventory of firmware versions and accounts; vendor tools (OpenManage, iLO RESTful API).

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: BMCs reachable from the production LAN with default credentials.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Dedicated management VLAN, unique credentials, firmware versions tracked.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Access only via MFA jump host, Redfish-driven firmware compliance, IPMI-over-LAN disabled, BMC configuration baselined and monitored.

controls.remediation_guidance: Move BMCs to an isolated management network, change all default credentials, disable IPMI-over-LAN or restrict it, patch firmware, and require access through a hardened jump host.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 PE family; ISO/IEC 27002:2022 clause 7; NIST SP 800-88 Rev.1 (media sanitization); vendor hardware hardening guides

controls.name: Removable media and unused ports are controlled
controls.objective: Reduce the risk of malware introduction and data removal through USB, optical, serial and console ports.
controls.business_justification: Removable media remains a path for malware delivery and unmonitored data exfiltration from servers.
controls.threat: Malware via removable media, boot from unauthorised media, data exfiltration.
controls.assessment_question: Are USB and removable-media ports, unused console ports and boot-from-removable options disabled or controlled on servers?
evidence_required: GPO, MDM, udev or USBGuard configuration
controls.validation_procedure:
Windows: `reg query HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\USBSTOR /v Start` (value 4 means disabled) and review the GPO "Removable Storage Access".
Linux: `lsmod | grep usb_storage`, `systemctl status usbguard`, `grep -r usb-storage /etc/modprobe.d/`.
Review UEFI boot order and boot-device password settings for a sample of physical servers.

automation.method: GPO or Intune export; Ansible or OpenSCAP check for a blacklisted usb-storage module.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Ports and boot options are open on all servers.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Removable storage blocked by policy, boot order locked, exceptions approved.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Device control enforced by EDR with alerts on blocked attempts, quarterly exception review.

controls.remediation_guidance: Block removable storage by policy, lock boot order with a firmware password, and use EDR device control with alerting where USB access is needed.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 PE family; ISO/IEC 27002:2022 clause 7; NIST SP 800-88 Rev.1 (media sanitization); vendor hardware hardening guides

controls.name: Storage media is sanitised or destroyed before replacement and disposal
controls.objective: Ensure data cannot be recovered from storage devices that are replaced, returned, re-used or retired.
controls.business_justification: Discarded drives and vendor returns are a recurring source of confidential data exposure and regulatory breaches.
controls.threat: Data recovery from discarded drives, leakage through vendor RMA returns.
controls.assessment_question: Is media containing confidential data sanitised to a recognised standard or destroyed, with certificates retained, before leaving the organisation or being re-used?
controls.validation_procedure:
Sample 5 retired or RMA-returned servers from the asset register and trace each to a sanitisation record or destruction certificate.
Confirm the sanitisation method meets NIST SP 800-88 (clear, purge or destroy) and that crypto-erase is evidenced where self-encrypting drives are used.
Review vendor contracts for media retention or "keep your drive" clauses.

automation.method: ITAM workflow that blocks asset closure without an attached sanitisation certificate.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Drives are discarded or returned without a defined process.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Documented sanitisation standard, certificates retained for most disposals.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Full-disk encryption plus crypto-erase on every retirement, automated closure checks, periodic vendor audits.

controls.remediation_guidance: Adopt a media sanitisation standard aligned to NIST SP 800-88, require certificates for every disposal, and add contract clauses for vendor-held media.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 PE family; ISO/IEC 27002:2022 clause 7; NIST SP 800-88 Rev.1 (media sanitization); vendor hardware hardening guides

controls.name: Secure configuration baselines are defined for every server platform
controls.objective: Ensure servers are built to an approved, hardened and documented configuration.
controls.business_justification: Insecure defaults and inconsistent builds are a leading cause of avoidable compromise and audit findings.
controls.threat: Exploitation of insecure defaults and misconfiguration.
controls.assessment_question: Is there an approved hardening baseline (for example CIS Benchmark level) for each server OS and role, and is it applied at build?
evidence_required: golden image or build pipeline definitions (Packer, MDT, Ansible, Terraform)
controls.validation_procedure:
Obtain baselines and confirm they track a current CIS Benchmark or Microsoft security baseline version.
Sample 5 servers and measure compliance. Windows: Microsoft Security Compliance Toolkit (Policy Analyzer) or CIS-CAT. Linux: `oscap xccdf eval --profile <cis-profile> --report out.html <ssg-datastream>` or `lynis audit system`.
Record the percentage of controls passed and review the exceptions register for approval and expiry.

automation.method: OpenSCAP, CIS-CAT or Lynis scheduled scans; Microsoft Defender for Cloud or Intune configuration assessment; Ansible check mode.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Servers are built manually from the vendor defaults.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Documented baselines per platform applied through build scripts, exceptions approved.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Baselines versioned as code, continuously assessed with automated compliance scoring, drift auto-remediated.

controls.remediation_guidance: Adopt a CIS or vendor baseline per platform, encode it in build automation, and track exceptions with expiry dates.
controls.references: CIS Benchmarks (Windows Server, RHEL, Ubuntu); Microsoft Security Baselines; DISA STIGs; NIST SP 800-123; NIST SP 800-70

controls.name: Configuration drift from the baseline is detected and corrected
controls.objective: Detect and remediate deviations from approved configurations in a timely way.
controls.business_justification: Unmanaged drift silently erodes hardening and can mask malicious modification.
controls.threat: Gradual misconfiguration, unauthorised changes, attacker persistence settings left unnoticed.
controls.assessment_question: Is compliance with the baseline continuously or periodically assessed, with deviations tracked to closure?
controls.validation_procedure:
Obtain the latest compliance scan and trend. Windows: `Get-DscConfigurationStatus` if DSC is used, or the Intune and Defender for Endpoint secure configuration export. Linux: `ansible-playbook site.yml --check --diff` or `aide --check`.
Select 3 failed items and verify each has an owner, a ticket and a remediation date.

automation.method: Scheduled OpenSCAP, Ansible check mode, Intune compliance reports, Defender for Cloud recommendations.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: No drift checks; configuration is reviewed only after incidents.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Periodic compliance scans with tracked remediation.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Continuous drift detection with automatic reversion and compliance trend reporting to management.

controls.remediation_guidance: Schedule automated baseline scans, route failures to owners via tickets, and auto-remediate low-risk drift.
controls.references: CIS Benchmarks (Windows Server, RHEL, Ubuntu); Microsoft Security Baselines; DISA STIGs; NIST SP 800-123; NIST SP 800-70

controls.name: Unnecessary services, roles, features and ports are disabled or removed
controls.objective: Minimise attack surface by running only what each server role requires.
controls.business_justification: Every unneeded service is an additional vulnerability and monitoring burden.
controls.threat: Exploitation of unused or legacy services (SMBv1, telnet, FTP, print spooler on non-print servers).
controls.assessment_question: Are all services, roles, features, protocols and listening ports not required by the server role disabled or removed?
evidence_required: Service and role inventory per server
controls.validation_procedure:
Windows: `Get-WindowsFeature | where Installed`, `Get-Service | where Status -eq Running`, `Get-NetTCPConnection -State Listen`, `Get-SmbServerConfiguration | select EnableSMB1Protocol`.
Linux: `systemctl list-unit-files --state=enabled`, `ss -tulpn`, and check for telnet, rsh and ftp packages with `rpm -qa` or `dpkg -l`.
Compare results with the documented role requirement and record unexplained services.

automation.method: osquery (listening_ports, services tables), Ansible facts, scheduled Nmap scans.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Default installs with all services enabled.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Role-based builds with documented service lists; periodic review.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Minimal images, automated detection of unauthorised services and ports with alerts.

controls.remediation_guidance: Build from minimal images, remove or disable unneeded services, and alert on newly listening ports.
controls.references: CIS Benchmarks (Windows Server, RHEL, Ubuntu); Microsoft Security Baselines; DISA STIGs; NIST SP 800-123; NIST SP 800-70

controls.name: An approved authorised-use banner is displayed at login
controls.objective: Establish a legal notice of authorised use at every administrative login interface.
controls.business_justification: A banner supports lawful monitoring and enforcement and is commonly required by regulators and insurers.
controls.threat: Disputed unauthorised-access enforcement and claims of implied consent.
controls.assessment_question: Do servers display a legally approved authorised-use notice at console, SSH, RDP and web administration logins?
evidence_required: screenshots of console, SSH and RDP logins
controls.validation_procedure:
Windows: `reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System" /v legalnoticetext`.
Linux: `sshd -T | grep -i banner` and `cat /etc/issue /etc/issue.net`.
Attempt a login to confirm the banner appears and record any interface where it is technically impossible.

automation.method: GPO export or Ansible lineinfile check.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: No banner configured.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Legal-approved banner deployed to all administrative interfaces.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Banner enforced as code with drift alerts and annual legal review.

controls.remediation_guidance: Obtain legal-approved wording and deploy it by GPO or configuration management to all login interfaces.
controls.references: CIS Benchmarks (Windows Server, RHEL, Ubuntu); Microsoft Security Baselines; DISA STIGs; NIST SP 800-123; NIST SP 800-70

controls.name: Boot chain integrity protections are enabled
controls.objective: Ensure the server only boots trusted firmware and operating system components.
controls.business_justification: Bootkits and firmware implants survive reinstallation and evade operating-system security tools.
controls.threat: Bootkits, firmware implants, boot from unauthorised media.
controls.assessment_question: Are Secure Boot, a UEFI/BIOS administrator password, TPM-backed measured boot and restricted boot order enabled on physical and virtual servers where supported?
evidence_required: Secure Boot and TPM status output
controls.validation_procedure:
Windows: `Confirm-SecureBootUEFI`, `Get-Tpm`, and msinfo32 (BIOS Mode UEFI, Secure Boot State On).
Linux: `mokutil --sb-state`, `ls /sys/firmware/efi`, and `tpm2_pcrread` where tpm2-tools is installed.
Hyper-V guests: `Get-VMFirmware -VMName <vm> | select SecureBoot`. List legacy-BIOS machines as exceptions.

automation.method: Defender for Endpoint or Intune device health attestation; osquery secureboot table; Redfish BIOS attributes.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Legacy BIOS boot with no firmware protection.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Secure Boot and firmware password on most servers, exceptions documented.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Measured boot with remote attestation and firmware settings monitored for change.

controls.remediation_guidance: Convert to UEFI, enable Secure Boot and TPM, set firmware passwords, and restrict boot devices.
controls.references: CIS Benchmarks (Windows Server, RHEL, Ubuntu); Microsoft Security Baselines; DISA STIGs; NIST SP 800-123; NIST SP 800-70

controls.name: Server configuration changes follow documented change control
controls.objective: Ensure changes are assessed, approved, tested and traceable.
controls.business_justification: Uncontrolled change causes outages and security regressions, and obscures malicious modification.
controls.threat: Unauthorised or untested changes, concealed malicious changes.
controls.assessment_question: Is there a documented change process for server configuration (request, risk review, approval, test, rollback, post-change review) and is it followed?
controls.validation_procedure:
Sample 10 recent system changes from the configuration repository or logs and trace each to an approved ticket (target 90% match or better).
Windows: `Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='Security';Id=4719}` (audit policy changes). Linux: `ausearch -k config_change`, `dnf history` or `/var/log/dpkg.log`.
Review emergency changes for after-the-fact approval.

automation.method: ITSM-to-CMDB reconciliation; Ansible Tower/AWX job logs; mandatory ticket reference in Git commits.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Changes made ad hoc by administrators.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Documented process with approval and testing; sampled evidence of compliance.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Pipeline-enforced change with automatic ticket linkage, metrics, and unauthorised-change alerting.

controls.remediation_guidance: Implement a change process with risk-based approval, rollback plans and automated reconciliation of detected changes to tickets.
controls.references: CIS Benchmarks (Windows Server, RHEL, Ubuntu); Microsoft Security Baselines; DISA STIGs; NIST SP 800-123; NIST SP 800-70

controls.name: Only authorised software can execute or be installed on servers
controls.objective: Prevent execution of unapproved binaries and scripts.
controls.business_justification: Application allow-listing blocks the majority of commodity malware and living-off-the-land tooling.
controls.threat: Ransomware and malware execution, attacker tooling, unauthorised software.
controls.assessment_question: Is application allow-listing or equivalent execution control enforced on servers, and is software installation restricted to approved administrators and sources?
controls.validation_procedure:
Windows: `Get-AppLockerPolicy -Effective -Xml` and `Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_DeviceGuard -Namespace root\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceGuard` (code integrity enforcement status).
Linux: `systemctl status fapolicyd`, `getenforce` or `aa-status`.
Compare the software inventory with the approved list and confirm policies are in enforce mode, not audit.

automation.method: Intune or GPO policy export; osquery programs table; EDR application control reports.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Any software can be installed or run.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Allow-listing enforced for critical servers, installs restricted.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Enforced allow-listing on all servers with managed exception workflow and violation alerting.

controls.remediation_guidance: Deploy WDAC/AppLocker or fapolicyd in audit mode, tune, then enforce; restrict installation rights.
controls.references: CIS Benchmarks (Windows Server, RHEL, Ubuntu); Microsoft Security Baselines; DISA STIGs; NIST SP 800-123; NIST SP 800-70

controls.name: A documented patch management process with risk-based timelines exists
controls.objective: Ensure operating systems, applications and firmware are patched within defined timeframes.
controls.business_justification: Known unpatched vulnerabilities remain the most common route to server compromise and ransomware.
controls.threat: Exploitation of known vulnerabilities.
controls.assessment_question: Is there a documented patch process defining roles, schedules, severity-based timelines, testing, exceptions and coverage of OS, applications and firmware?
evidence_required: records from two recent patch cycles
controls.validation_procedure:
Review the policy for timelines by severity and exploitation status, and for coverage of third-party applications, firmware and hypervisors.
Sample the last two patch cycles: scope versus asset inventory, approvals, test evidence and deployment rate.
Confirm where the process is documented and who owns it.

automation.method: WSUS, Intune, Update Manager or Red Hat Satellite compliance exports via API.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Patching is ad hoc and left to individual administrators.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Documented process and calendar, timelines defined, most servers patched in time.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Automated patching with measured timelines, exception governance and threat-led acceleration.

controls.remediation_guidance: Define severity and exploitability-based patch timelines, assign ownership, and automate deployment with compliance reporting.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-40 Rev.4; CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog; vendor lifecycle and support policies

controls.name: Patch currency is verified per server and installation failures are resolved
controls.objective: Know the real patch level of each server and detect failed or pending installations.
controls.business_justification: Reported patch compliance often overstates reality when failures and pending reboots go unnoticed.
controls.threat: Unpatched systems believed to be compliant.
controls.assessment_question: Can the organisation show the current patch level per server, and are failed or pending installations detected and resolved?
controls.validation_procedure:
Windows: `Get-HotFix | sort InstalledOn -Descending | select -First 10`; pending reboot via registry key `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Component Based Servicing\RebootPending`.
Linux: `apt list --upgradable` or `dnf updateinfo list security`; `needs-restarting -r` or `/var/run/reboot-required`.
Compare results with the console report and timelines; sample failed installs against tickets.

automation.method: Patch console exports, Defender TVM, Nessus credentialed patch audit plugins.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Patch level is unknown outside manual checks.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Per-server patch inventory with failure monitoring.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Automated reconciliation of console data and scanner results, failures auto-ticketed.

controls.remediation_guidance: Reconcile patch tooling reports against credentialed scans, auto-ticket failures, and track pending reboots.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-40 Rev.4; CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog; vendor lifecycle and support policies

controls.name: Unsupported and end-of-life systems are governed through approved exceptions
controls.objective: Prevent unsupported platforms from running without compensating controls and a retirement plan.
controls.business_justification: End-of-life systems receive no security fixes and are routinely used for initial access and lateral movement.
controls.threat: Unpatchable vulnerabilities in end-of-life operating systems and applications.
controls.assessment_question: Are operating systems and applications beyond vendor support identified and either removed, isolated, or covered by a time-bound, risk-accepted exception with compensating controls?
evidence_required: exception register with approvals and expiry
controls.validation_procedure:
Windows: `Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem | select Caption,Version`. Linux: `cat /etc/os-release`.
Compare every server against the vendor lifecycle (vendor pages or endoflife.date), for example Windows Server 2012 R2 or CentOS 7.
For each end-of-life host, verify an approved exception, an expiry date, and isolation or monitoring as compensating controls.

automation.method: CMDB lifecycle fields plus scanner "unsupported operating system" findings.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Unsupported systems are unknown or unmanaged.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Inventory of end-of-life systems with approved, dated exceptions.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Lifecycle-driven roadmap, no unmanaged end-of-life systems, automatic alerts ahead of support end.

controls.remediation_guidance: Inventory support dates, migrate or isolate end-of-life hosts, and require time-bound exceptions signed by the risk owner.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-40 Rev.4; CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog; vendor lifecycle and support policies

controls.name: Emergency patching exists for actively exploited and critical vulnerabilities
controls.objective: Compress time-to-remediate for vulnerabilities with known exploitation.
controls.business_justification: Exploits are often weaponised within days of disclosure; routine cycles are too slow for these cases.
controls.threat: Rapid exploitation of newly disclosed vulnerabilities.
controls.assessment_question: Is there a tested fast-track process for actively exploited or critical vulnerabilities (including CISA KEV entries), with timelines that are measured and met?
controls.validation_procedure:
Select 3 recent KEV or critical CVEs affecting the estate and measure disclosure-to-remediation time per server.
Compare with the target. The source checklist required remediation of CVSS 7 or higher within one business day; this framework recommends risk-based targets (for example internet-facing KEV within 72 hours).
Verify mitigations for systems that cannot be patched immediately.

automation.method: KEV feed correlated with scanner or Defender TVM asset data.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: No emergency process; critical patches wait for the monthly cycle.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Defined fast-track with owners; usually met for internet-facing systems.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Threat-intel triggered automation with measured, consistently met targets.

controls.remediation_guidance: Subscribe to KEV and vendor advisories, define emergency timelines by exposure, and rehearse the process.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-40 Rev.4; CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog; vendor lifecycle and support policies

controls.name: Firmware and hypervisor layers are inventoried and patched
controls.objective: Keep BIOS/UEFI, BMC, controller, NIC firmware and hypervisor builds current.
controls.business_justification: Firmware and hypervisor flaws affect every workload above them and are often missed by OS patching.
controls.threat: Firmware implants, hypervisor escape and ESXi-targeting ransomware exploits.
controls.assessment_question: Are firmware and hypervisor versions inventoried and patched on a managed cadence?
evidence_required: hypervisor build numbers versus vendor advisories
controls.validation_procedure:
VMware: `Get-VMHost | select Name,Version,Build` (PowerCLI). Hyper-V: `Get-ComputerInfo`. Proxmox: `pveversion -v`.
Redfish: `curl -k -u <user> https://<bmc>/redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory`.
Compare against current vendor security advisories and note hosts behind the supported builds.

automation.method: Redfish and vendor management APIs; PowerCLI scheduled reports.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Firmware is never updated after installation.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Annual firmware cycle and tracked hypervisor patching.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Continuous firmware compliance reporting and risk-based expedited updates.

controls.remediation_guidance: Inventory firmware and hypervisor versions, subscribe to vendor advisories, and schedule updates with maintenance windows.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-40 Rev.4; CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog; vendor lifecycle and support policies

controls.name: Security-relevant events are logged on every server
controls.objective: Generate the audit trail needed to detect and investigate compromise.
controls.business_justification: Without logs, intrusions cannot be detected, scoped or proven, and regulatory obligations cannot be met.
controls.threat: Undetected compromise and loss of forensic evidence.
controls.assessment_question: Are authentication, privilege use, account and group changes, access-control changes, scheduled job and service creation, and system integrity events logged with timestamps?
controls.validation_procedure:
Windows: `auditpol /get /category:*`; `Get-WinEvent -ListLog Security | select LogName,MaximumSizeInBytes`; confirm events 4624, 4625, 4672, 4720, 4728, 4732, 4697, 4698 and 7045 occur; check PowerShell script block logging at `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\ScriptBlockLogging`.
Linux: `systemctl is-active auditd`, `auditctl -l` (look for rules on /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, sudoers and execve), `last -n 20`.

automation.method: GPO and auditd configuration exports; Ansible audit role; osquery event tables.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Default logging only.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Defined audit policy applied consistently with timestamps and critical events covered.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Threat-informed audit policy (including command-line and script logging) validated by detection tests.

controls.remediation_guidance: Enable advanced audit policy, auditd rules and PowerShell logging aligned to a documented logging standard.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-92; CIS Control 8; Microsoft Windows auditing guidance; CISA/ASD logging best-practice guidance

controls.name: Logs are forwarded in near real time to a central tamper-resistant store
controls.objective: Preserve evidence off-host and detect log tampering or forwarding failure.
controls.business_justification: Attackers routinely clear local logs; central storage preserves evidence and enables correlation.
controls.threat: Log clearing, loss of evidence, single point of failure on the host.
controls.assessment_question: Are logs forwarded in near real time to a central, access-restricted platform, with alerts when forwarding stops or logs are cleared?
evidence_required: forwarder configuration (WEF/WEC, Azure Monitor Agent, rsyslog, Splunk UF)
alert rules for log clearing and silent sources
controls.validation_procedure:
Windows: `wecutil gs <subscription>` or check the agent service. Linux: `grep -R "omfwd" /etc/rsyslog.conf /etc/rsyslog.d/`.
In the SIEM, verify last-event time per server (stale beyond 15 minutes is a gap).
Generate benign test events: `logger -p auth.notice "SAOS-test"` and `eventcreate /T INFORMATION /ID 999 /L APPLICATION /SO SAOS /D "test"`, then confirm arrival.
Confirm an alert exists for Security log cleared (event 1102).

automation.method: SIEM API for last-seen per source; synthetic heartbeat events.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Logs remain only on local servers.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Central collection for most servers with documented coverage.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Complete coverage with write-once storage, heartbeat monitoring and log-clear alerts.

controls.remediation_guidance: Deploy forwarders to all servers, send to a restricted SIEM or log store, and alert on silent sources and log clearing.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-92; CIS Control 8; Microsoft Windows auditing guidance; CISA/ASD logging best-practice guidance

controls.name: Log retention satisfies investigation and regulatory needs
controls.objective: Keep logs long enough to investigate incidents that are discovered late.
controls.business_justification: Intrusions are often found weeks after initial access; short retention destroys the evidence needed to scope them.
controls.threat: Loss of forensic evidence when local logs roll over.
controls.assessment_question: Is log retention (online and archive) defined to meet investigation and regulatory requirements, and are local log sizes sufficient to prevent early overwrite?
controls.validation_procedure:
Windows: `wevtutil gl Security` (maxSize and retention). Linux: `journalctl --disk-usage` and `grep -E 'max_log_file|num_logs' /etc/audit/auditd.conf`.
Confirm the SIEM can return events older than the required window. The source checklist required at least 2 weeks locally; this framework recommends at least 90 days online and 12 months archived, subject to regulation.

automation.method: SIEM retention API; scripted check of oldest available event per source.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Logs overwrite quickly with no retention requirement.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Retention defined and configured to policy.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Tiered retention aligned to regulation and threat profile, validated by periodic retrieval tests.

controls.remediation_guidance: Set minimum retention (online and archive) by data class and regulation, and size local logs to cover forwarding outages.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-92; CIS Control 8; Microsoft Windows auditing guidance; CISA/ASD logging best-practice guidance

controls.name: Sensitive data is excluded from logs and log files are protected
controls.objective: Prevent logs from becoming a store of credentials or personal data.
controls.business_justification: Credentials and personal data in logs create breach exposure and privacy compliance failures.
controls.threat: Credential exposure through logs and privacy breaches.
controls.assessment_question: Is logging configured to exclude passwords, secrets, tokens and sensitive personal data, and are log files access-restricted?
controls.validation_procedure:
Windows: review process command-line auditing (event 4688) and PowerShell transcripts for secrets.
Linux: `grep -riE "password=|passwd|secret|token" /var/log 2>/dev/null | head` and `ls -l /var/log`.
With authorisation, run `gitleaks detect --no-git -s /var/log` or `trufflehog filesystem /var/log`.

automation.method: Secret scanners against log stores; SIEM masking and data-loss rules.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Logs contain secrets and are world-readable.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Logging standard prohibits sensitive data and permissions are restricted.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Automated secret scanning of logs with masking at source.

controls.remediation_guidance: Mask sensitive fields at source, restrict log permissions, and scan log stores for secrets.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-92; CIS Control 8; Microsoft Windows auditing guidance; CISA/ASD logging best-practice guidance

controls.name: Log monitoring and alert triage run on a defined schedule and are reviewed for effectiveness
controls.objective: Ensure collected logs are actually examined and that monitoring quality is measured.
controls.business_justification: Logs that are never reviewed give a false sense of assurance.
controls.threat: Missed intrusions despite available evidence.
controls.assessment_question: Is there a documented, scheduled monitoring and triage process with defined detection use cases, ownership, and an effectiveness review at least monthly?
controls.validation_procedure:
Review the procedure and schedule and sample 3 months of review evidence.
Select 5 use cases (new local administrator, service creation, failed-logon spike, audit log cleared, new SSH key) and trigger benign test events.
Verify alerts fire, are triaged and result in tickets within the target time.

automation.method: SIEM detection rules as code; purple-team or Atomic Red Team test execution.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: No defined monitoring; logs reviewed only after incidents.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Documented schedule and use cases with evidence of triage.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Measured detection coverage against ATT&CK with regular testing and tuning.

controls.remediation_guidance: Define server detection use cases, assign monitoring ownership, and review detection performance monthly.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-92; CIS Control 8; Microsoft Windows auditing guidance; CISA/ASD logging best-practice guidance

controls.name: Servers use authoritative time and name-resolution sources
controls.objective: Ensure consistent time for log correlation and authentication, and trustworthy name resolution.
controls.business_justification: Inconsistent time breaks forensic timelines and Kerberos; untrusted DNS enables redirection attacks.
controls.threat: Log correlation failure, authentication failures, DNS spoofing.
controls.assessment_question: Do all servers synchronise time from authoritative, resilient sources and use authorised DNS resolvers?
controls.validation_procedure:
Windows: `w32tm /query /status`, `w32tm /query /source`, `Get-DnsClientServerAddress` (domain members should follow the domain hierarchy; the PDC emulator syncs to a reliable external source).
Linux: `chronyc sources -v`, `timedatectl show`, `resolvectl status` or `cat /etc/resolv.conf`.
Confirm clock offset is well under one second and resolvers are the approved internal servers.

automation.method: Fleet-wide chrony/w32tm offset reports; DNS configuration compliance checks.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Clocks drift and resolvers are set arbitrarily.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Authoritative time and DNS sources defined and configured.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Redundant authenticated time sources with offset monitoring and alerts.

controls.remediation_guidance: Standardise time sources and resolvers in the build baseline and monitor clock offset.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-92; CIS Control 8; Microsoft Windows auditing guidance; CISA/ASD logging best-practice guidance

controls.name: Anti-malware or EDR is deployed, current and tamper-protected on servers
controls.objective: Detect and block malicious code and behaviour on servers.
controls.business_justification: Servers are prime ransomware targets; endpoint protection is a baseline expectation of insurers and regulators.
controls.threat: Malware and ransomware execution, defence tampering.
controls.assessment_question: Is anti-malware or EDR installed on all servers with real-time protection, current signatures and engine, tamper protection, and monitored alerts?
controls.validation_procedure:
Windows: `Get-MpComputerStatus | select AMServiceEnabled,RealTimeProtectionEnabled,AntivirusSignatureLastUpdated,IsTamperProtected` and `Get-MpPreference | select ExclusionPath,ExclusionProcess`.
Linux: `mdatp health` for Defender, or the vendor equivalent.
Compare EDR-reported hosts with the inventory and review exclusions for breadth and approval.

automation.method: EDR console API coverage report; Defender for Endpoint device inventory.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Protection absent or unmanaged on many servers.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Deployed on all servers with updates and central alerting.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Tamper-protected EDR on all servers with reviewed exclusions and response playbooks.

controls.remediation_guidance: Deploy EDR to every server, enable tamper protection, and review exclusions quarterly.
controls.references: CIS Controls 10 and 13; Microsoft Defender documentation; vendor EDR hardening guides

controls.name: A host firewall enforces default-deny inbound rules
controls.objective: Limit network access to each server to required services and sources.
controls.business_justification: Host firewalls contain lateral movement when perimeter and segmentation controls fail.
controls.threat: Lateral movement and service exposure.
controls.assessment_question: Is a host firewall enabled in default-deny inbound mode with rules limited to required services and management sources?
controls.validation_procedure:
Windows: `Get-NetFirewallProfile | select Name,Enabled,DefaultInboundAction` and `Get-NetFirewallRule -Enabled True -Direction Inbound -Action Allow | select DisplayName,Profile`.
Linux: `firewall-cmd --list-all`, `nft list ruleset`, `ufw status verbose` or `iptables -S`.
Confirm the default inbound policy is block or drop and that rules restrict source addresses.

automation.method: GPO, Intune or Ansible firewall policy export; OpenSCAP firewall rules.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Host firewall disabled.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Enabled with default-deny and role-based rules.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Source-restricted rules managed as code with periodic review and drift alerts.

controls.remediation_guidance: Enable the host firewall in default-deny mode and scope rules to required ports and sources.
controls.references: CIS Controls 10 and 13; Microsoft Defender documentation; vendor EDR hardening guides

controls.name: Host intrusion prevention and exploit mitigations are enabled
controls.objective: Block exploitation techniques and malicious behaviour at the host.
controls.business_justification: Prevention-mode controls on authentication servers protect the systems that hold the keys to the whole estate.
controls.threat: Memory-corruption exploitation and post-exploitation behaviour.
controls.assessment_question: Are host intrusion prevention and OS exploit mitigations enabled, and mandatory in prevention mode on authentication servers (domain controllers, identity providers, RADIUS, PAM)?
evidence_required: list of authentication servers with HIPS status
controls.validation_procedure:
Windows: `Get-ProcessMitigation -System` and `Get-MpPreference | select -ExpandProperty AttackSurfaceReductionRules_Ids`.
Linux: `sestatus` or `aa-status`, and `sysctl kernel.randomize_va_space kernel.kptr_restrict`.
Confirm authentication servers run in prevention mode, not detect-only.

automation.method: Defender ASR rule reporting; EDR policy export; OpenSCAP kernel hardening checks.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: No host prevention capability.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Prevention enabled on critical and authentication servers.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Tuned prevention on all servers with measured block events and regular tests.

controls.remediation_guidance: Enable exploit mitigations and ASR rules, and enforce prevention mode on authentication servers.
controls.references: CIS Controls 10 and 13; Microsoft Defender documentation; vendor EDR hardening guides

controls.name: File and configuration integrity monitoring covers critical system paths
controls.objective: Detect unauthorised changes to system binaries, configuration and sensitive files.
controls.business_justification: Integrity monitoring detects web shells, rootkits and persistence that signature tools miss.
controls.threat: Web shells, binary tampering, rootkits, persistence mechanisms.
controls.assessment_question: Is file and configuration integrity monitoring in place for critical system files, binaries, configuration and registry paths, with alerting on unauthorised change?
controls.validation_procedure:
Linux: `aide --check` or `tripwire --check`; confirm the AIDE database is stored read-only or off-host.
Windows: Defender for Endpoint, Wazuh or Tripwire FIM; Sysmon events 11, 12 and 13 for file and registry activity.
Make a controlled benign change to a monitored test file and confirm an alert is raised.

automation.method: Wazuh, AIDE, Tripwire or EDR FIM with SIEM alerting.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: No integrity monitoring.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: FIM on critical servers and paths with alerts.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Comprehensive FIM with change-ticket correlation and automated triage.

controls.remediation_guidance: Deploy FIM on critical paths, protect baselines off-host, and correlate alerts with approved changes.
controls.references: CIS Controls 10 and 13; Microsoft Defender documentation; vendor EDR hardening guides

controls.name: Servers are hardened and vulnerability-assessed before entering production
controls.objective: Ensure no server goes live with known exploitable weaknesses or without a retained security baseline.
controls.business_justification: Fixing issues before go-live is far cheaper than after exposure, and the baseline report supports later audits and investigations.
controls.threat: Insecure systems exposed at go-live.
controls.assessment_question: Is every new or rebuilt server configuration-reviewed and vulnerability-scanned before production, and are the baseline reports retained?
evidence_required: pre-production scan and baseline compliance report
controls.validation_procedure:
Sample 5 servers deployed in the last 12 months and locate the pre-production scan report, the open findings by severity at go-live, and the approval of any residual risk.
For automated builds, confirm a scan gate exists in the pipeline.
Verify reports are retained and retrievable.

automation.method: Pipeline gate calling a scanner API (Nessus, Qualys, Defender TVM, OpenVAS).

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Servers go live without assessment.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Pre-production checklist and scan completed with sign-off and retained reports.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Automated pipeline gates block deployment on policy failure with exception workflow.

controls.remediation_guidance: Add a mandatory pre-production hardening and scanning gate with documented sign-off and report retention.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-115; NIST SP 800-40 Rev.4; CVSS specification (FIRST); EPSS; CISA KEV catalog

controls.name: Servers receive recurring credentialed vulnerability scans
controls.objective: Continuously identify missing patches and misconfigurations across all servers.
controls.business_justification: Unauthenticated scans miss most local vulnerabilities; coverage gaps leave unknown risk.
controls.threat: Unknown vulnerabilities and false negatives from unauthenticated scanning.
controls.assessment_question: Are all servers scanned with credentialed scans at a defined frequency (at least monthly, weekly for internet-facing), and are coverage gaps tracked?
controls.validation_procedure:
Export the scanner asset list and compare with the inventory (target coverage of 95% or better).
Check the authentication success rate per scan and the last-scanned date per server.
Confirm internet-facing assets are also scanned externally from an authorised host (`nmap -sV <public-ip>`).

automation.method: Scanner API coverage reports reconciled to CMDB.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: No regular scanning.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Scheduled credentialed scans with tracked coverage.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Continuous assessment (agent-based) with near-complete coverage and exposure-aware prioritisation.

controls.remediation_guidance: Schedule credentialed scans for all servers, fix authentication failures, and scan internet-facing assets externally.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-115; NIST SP 800-40 Rev.4; CVSS specification (FIRST); EPSS; CISA KEV catalog

controls.name: Vulnerability scanning is formally authorised and scanning tools are governed
controls.objective: Ensure scanning is permitted, unobstructed and performed only by approved people and tools.
controls.business_justification: Blocked scanners create blind spots, while unmanaged scanners and their credentials are an attack path.
controls.threat: Blind spots from blocked scanners, rogue scanning, scanner credential abuse.
controls.assessment_question: Is scanning formally authorised, are approved scanners excluded from blocking without blanket whitelisting, and are only approved tools and operators used?
evidence_required: Scanning authorisation or rules of engagement
controls.validation_procedure:
Review the authorisation and approved-tool list.
Confirm scanner IPs and service accounts are inventoried, least-privilege, vaulted and monitored, and that scanner subnets are not permanently exempt across the detection stack.
Hunt in the EDR for scanning tools (nmap, nessus) running outside approved hosts.

automation.method: EDR hunting query for unapproved scanner binaries.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Scanning occurs ad hoc with no approval or governance.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Authorised scanning with approved tools and operators.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Vaulted scanner credentials with monitored use and annual authorisation review.

controls.remediation_guidance: Document scanning authorisation, vault scanner credentials, and review exemptions in security tooling.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-115; NIST SP 800-40 Rev.4; CVSS specification (FIRST); EPSS; CISA KEV catalog

controls.name: Vulnerabilities are prioritised by risk, remediated within timelines and verified by rescan
controls.objective: Reduce exploitable exposure through risk-based prioritisation and closed-loop remediation.
controls.business_justification: CVSS alone misprioritises; combining exploitability, exposure and asset criticality focuses effort where breach likelihood is highest.
controls.threat: Backlog of exploitable issues and false closure of findings.
controls.assessment_question: Are vulnerabilities prioritised using severity, exploitability (CVSS, EPSS, KEV), asset criticality and exposure, with timelines enforced, exceptions approved and fixes verified by rescan?
controls.validation_procedure:
Export open vulnerabilities and calculate the percentage within timeline by severity.
Sample 10 closed items for rescan evidence and 5 exceptions for approval, compensating controls and expiry.
Where no CVSS exists, confirm the vulnerability is assessed for remote exploitability.

automation.method: Scanner and ticketing integration; KEV and EPSS enrichment.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Vulnerabilities are listed but not tracked to closure.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Defined timelines, tracked remediation and approved exceptions.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Risk-based prioritisation using threat data with measured, consistently met timelines and verified closure.

controls.remediation_guidance: Adopt risk-based timelines, enrich findings with KEV and EPSS, and require rescan validation before closure.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-115; NIST SP 800-40 Rev.4; CVSS specification (FIRST); EPSS; CISA KEV catalog

controls.name: Servers are placed in segmented zones with documented and minimised network exposure
controls.objective: Restrict network reachability of servers to required flows and prevent unintended exposure.
controls.business_justification: Flat networks turn a single compromised host into an enterprise-wide incident.
controls.threat: Lateral movement across flat networks and internet exposure of management or database ports.
controls.assessment_question: Are servers placed in zones appropriate to function and data sensitivity, with traffic limited to documented flows, no unintended internet exposure, and safeguards for specialised or shared computing (HPC, grid) environments?
evidence_required: firewall rule exports for server zones
controls.validation_procedure:
Compare the server inventory with VLAN and zone assignment.
Run an authorised external scan (`nmap -Pn -sV -p- <public-ranges>`) and compare to documented exposure.
From a user VLAN test reachability to admin ports (`Test-NetConnection <ip> -Port 3389` or `nc -vz <ip> 22`; also 445, 5985, 5986).
Review firewall rules for any-any and unused entries, and confirm HPC or grid workloads have documented safeguards.

automation.method: Firewall rule analysis tools (Tufin, AlgoSec, FireMon) or exported configuration parsing; external attack-surface management.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Flat network with servers and users together.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Defined server zones with documented flows and firewall control.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Micro-segmentation, continuous exposure monitoring and validated segmentation tests.

controls.remediation_guidance: Segment server zones, document flows, remove unused rules, and monitor external exposure continuously.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-41 Rev.1; NIST SP 800-207; CIS Control 12

controls.name: Default accounts and credentials are changed, renamed or disabled
controls.objective: Eliminate publicly known credentials on operating systems, applications and appliances.
controls.business_justification: Default credentials are trivially guessed and are tested first in nearly every attack.
controls.threat: Credential guessing with documented vendor defaults.
controls.assessment_question: Have all manufacturer and default accounts and passwords been changed, renamed or disabled on operating systems, applications, databases, BMCs and appliances?
evidence_required: BMC and appliance credential rotation records
controls.validation_procedure:
Windows: `Get-LocalUser | select Name,Enabled,PasswordLastSet`; confirm the built-in Administrator is renamed, disabled or LAPS-managed and Guest is disabled.
Linux: `awk -F: '($2==""){print $1}' /etc/shadow` and `getent passwd | awk -F: '$3==0{print $1}'`; check default application accounts (tomcat, admin, postgres, sa).
Run an authorised default-password scan (for example Nessus default-password plugins).

automation.method: Credentialed scanner default-password checks; Ansible account audit.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Default credentials remain on some systems.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Default accounts changed at build with a verified checklist.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Automated detection of default credentials with rotation to a vault.

controls.remediation_guidance: Change or disable default credentials during build, and scan for them regularly.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-63B; NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 AC and IA families; CIS Controls 5 and 6; Windows LAPS documentation

controls.name: Strong authentication is enforced for all administrative and root access
controls.objective: Protect administrative access with phishing-resistant or multi-factor authentication.
controls.business_justification: Stolen or guessed administrator passwords give full control of the server and often the domain.
controls.threat: Password theft, brute force and reuse against privileged accounts.
controls.assessment_question: Is MFA or equivalent strong authentication (smart card, FIDO2, key-based SSH with passphrase) enforced for every administrator and root-level access?
evidence_required: MFA and Conditional Access policy export
controls.validation_procedure:
Windows: confirm admin RDP and console logon occurs through a PAW or jump host with MFA (Conditional Access, smart card or Windows Hello for Business); `Get-ADUser -Filter {SmartcardLogonRequired -eq $true}` for smart-card-enforced admins.
Linux: `sshd -T | egrep "passwordauthentication|permitrootlogin|pubkeyauthentication|authenticationmethods"` and `grep -E "pam_google_authenticator|pam_duo" /etc/pam.d/sshd`.
Compare the admin list with enforcement and attempt a password-only login (expect failure).

automation.method: Entra sign-in logs and Conditional Access reports; sshd -T compliance scan.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Passwords only for administrators.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: MFA enforced for administrators with documented exceptions.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Phishing-resistant MFA everywhere with just-in-time elevation and no standing access.

controls.remediation_guidance: Enforce MFA via jump host or PAM, move SSH to keys or certificates, and remove password-only paths.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-63B; NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 AC and IA families; CIS Controls 5 and 6; Windows LAPS documentation

controls.name: Access to the server, applications and data follows least privilege
controls.objective: Restrict access to authorised, authenticated users with only the rights they need.
controls.business_justification: Excess privilege multiplies the damage of any single account compromise or insider misuse.
controls.threat: Excess privilege enabling data theft, sabotage and privilege escalation.
controls.assessment_question: Is access limited to authorised, authenticated users through role-based groups with least privilege, and without direct user permissions on resources?
evidence_required: local and domain group membership exports
controls.validation_procedure:
Windows: `Get-LocalGroupMember Administrators`, `Get-SmbShare | Get-SmbShareAccess`, `icacls <path>`; look for Everyone or Authenticated Users write access.
Linux: `getent group sudo wheel`, `find / -xdev -perm -0002 -type f 2>/dev/null | head`, `find / -xdev -perm -4000 -type f`.
Sample 10 users and compare their rights with job roles.

automation.method: AD and local group exports; access analytics tools; Ansible user audit.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Broad shared access with many administrators.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Role-based groups and documented access matrix.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Just-in-time elevation, automated entitlement analytics and periodic recertification.

controls.remediation_guidance: Move to role-based groups, remove direct and excessive permissions, and recertify access quarterly.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-63B; NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 AC and IA families; CIS Controls 5 and 6; Windows LAPS documentation

controls.name: Access is granted, changed and removed through a documented process with periodic review
controls.objective: Keep access aligned with current role and eliminate orphaned accounts.
controls.business_justification: Leavers and movers retaining access are a major source of audit findings and insider breaches.
controls.threat: Orphaned and over-provisioned access.
controls.assessment_question: Is there a documented process to grant, change and remove server access (joiner, mover, leaver), with periodic recertification of privileged and sensitive access?
controls.validation_procedure:
Sample 10 leavers and 10 movers and verify revocation within the target time (for example 24 hours).
Compare the HR leaver list with server and AD accounts.
Windows: `Get-ADUser -Filter {Enabled -eq $true} -Properties LastLogonDate | where LastLogonDate -lt (Get-Date).AddDays(-90)`. Linux: `lastlog -b 90`.
Check the date and outcome of the last recertification.

automation.method: HR-to-IAM leaver reconciliation; dormant account reports.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Access removed only when someone remembers.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Documented joiner/mover/leaver process with annual reviews.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: HR-driven automated provisioning and revocation with quarterly privileged recertification.

controls.remediation_guidance: Automate leaver revocation, disable dormant accounts, and recertify privileged access at least quarterly.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-63B; NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 AC and IA families; CIS Controls 5 and 6; Windows LAPS documentation

controls.name: Generic, shared and guest interactive accounts are disabled
controls.objective: Ensure every interactive session is attributable to one individual.
controls.business_justification: Shared accounts remove accountability and are hard to revoke when staff leave.
controls.threat: Loss of accountability and widely known shared credentials.
controls.assessment_question: Are generic, shared and guest accounts that permit interactive logon disabled, with any exception approved, attributable and logged (service accounts excluded)?
controls.validation_procedure:
Windows: `Get-LocalUser Guest`; review interactive logon events (4624 logon types 2 and 10) for non-personal accounts.
Linux: `getent passwd` for UID 1000 and above and `last` for shared names.
Verify exceptions use PAM checkout with session recording.

automation.method: Account inventory scripts with naming convention checks.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Shared admin accounts are common.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Shared accounts disabled apart from approved, logged exceptions.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: No shared accounts; break-glass access vaulted, alerted and reviewed after use.

controls.remediation_guidance: Replace shared accounts with named accounts and vault break-glass credentials.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-63B; NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 AC and IA families; CIS Controls 5 and 6; Windows LAPS documentation

controls.name: Trust relationships are identified, justified and reviewed
controls.objective: Know and control the implicit trust paths between systems and identities.
controls.business_justification: Unreviewed trusts allow an attacker to move from a low-value system to critical ones.
controls.threat: Lateral movement through unmonitored trust paths.
controls.assessment_question: Are all trust relationships (domain and forest trusts, SSH key trust, delegation, database links, service-to-service trust) identified, justified and reviewed?
controls.validation_procedure:
AD: `Get-ADTrust -Filter * | select Name,Direction,TrustType,SIDFilteringQuarantined` and `Get-ADComputer -Filter {TrustedForDelegation -eq $true}`.
Linux: `find /home /root -name authorized_keys`, `cat /etc/hosts.equiv ~/.rhosts 2>/dev/null`, and review `/etc/sudoers.d`.
Validate business justification, SID filtering and key ownership.

automation.method: AD trust and delegation reports; SSH key inventory scripts.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Trust relationships are unknown.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Trusts documented and reviewed annually.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Continuously monitored trust graph with automated alerts for new trusts and keys.

controls.remediation_guidance: Inventory trusts and delegation, remove unneeded ones, enable SID filtering, and review SSH keys.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-63B; NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 AC and IA families; CIS Controls 5 and 6; Windows LAPS documentation

controls.name: Local administrator and root credentials are unique, rotated and vaulted
controls.objective: Stop credential reuse of local privileged accounts across servers.
controls.business_justification: A shared local administrator password lets an attacker move across the whole estate from one stolen hash.
controls.threat: Pass-the-hash and credential reuse.
controls.assessment_question: Are local administrator and root credentials unique per server, automatically rotated and stored in a vault or LAPS, with access audited?
controls.validation_procedure:
Windows: `Get-LapsADPassword -Identity <server>` (Windows LAPS) or check legacy attributes with `Get-ADComputer -Filter * -Properties ms-Mcs-AdmPwdExpirationTime`.
Review who can read the password attribute (ACL review).
Linux: confirm root password rotation through a vault, or that direct root login is disabled.

automation.method: LAPS coverage report; PAM vault API.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: The same local administrator password is used on many servers.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: LAPS or vault deployed to most servers with controlled retrieval.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Full coverage with rotation after use and alerts on retrieval.

controls.remediation_guidance: Deploy Windows LAPS or a PAM vault, restrict who can read passwords, and disable direct root logon.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-63B; NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 AC and IA families; CIS Controls 5 and 6; Windows LAPS documentation

controls.name: Service accounts are inventoried, owned, least-privileged and protected
controls.objective: Control non-human identities that run services and scheduled jobs.
controls.business_justification: Service accounts are frequently over-privileged and never rotated, making them prime targets.
controls.threat: Kerberoasting, over-privileged service credentials, secret theft.
controls.assessment_question: Are service accounts inventoried with owners, non-interactive, least-privileged, and using managed identities, gMSA or vaulted secrets with rotation?
controls.validation_procedure:
AD: `Get-ADServiceAccount -Filter *` and `Get-ADUser -Filter {ServicePrincipalName -like "*"} -Properties PasswordLastSet,ServicePrincipalName`.
Windows services: `Get-CimInstance Win32_Service | select Name,StartName`.
Linux: review systemd units for `User=root`; `getent passwd | awk -F: '$7!~/nologin|false/'`.
Verify interactive logon rights are denied and membership of privileged groups is justified.

automation.method: AD service account reports; PAM discovery.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Service accounts are unknown and use shared passwords.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Register with owners and password rotation for critical accounts.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Managed identities and gMSA throughout, with anomaly detection on service account use.

controls.remediation_guidance: Inventory service accounts, move to gMSA or managed identities, rotate secrets, and deny interactive logon.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-63B; NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 AC and IA families; CIS Controls 5 and 6; Windows LAPS documentation

controls.name: Root login and privilege escalation on Linux are restricted and logged
controls.objective: Control how administrators gain root so that elevated actions are limited and attributable.
controls.business_justification: Unrestricted sudo or direct root login removes accountability and eases privilege escalation.
controls.threat: Privilege escalation through sudo misconfiguration and unaccountable root activity.
controls.assessment_question: Is direct root login restricted, and is sudo or PAM-based escalation limited to required commands, logged and free of NOPASSWD ALL rules?
controls.validation_procedure:
`sshd -T | grep permitrootlogin`, `grep -R "NOPASSWD\|ALL=(ALL" /etc/sudoers /etc/sudoers.d`, `visudo -c`.
Check sudo I/O logging with `grep -i "log_input\|log_output" /etc/sudoers*` and lockout with `grep pam_faillock /etc/pam.d/*`.
Windows analogue: `reg query HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System /v EnableLUA`.

automation.method: OpenSCAP and Ansible audits of sudoers and sshd.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Direct root login and unrestricted sudo.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Root login disabled and sudo restricted by role.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Just-in-time privilege with session recording and command-level auditing.

controls.remediation_guidance: Disable direct root SSH, scope sudo rules, require authentication, and log all elevated commands.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-63B; NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 AC and IA families; CIS Controls 5 and 6; Windows LAPS documentation

controls.name: Only secure protocols are used for administration and credential transmission
controls.objective: Protect administrative sessions and credentials from interception and downgrade.
controls.business_justification: Cleartext or weak administrative protocols expose credentials to anyone on the network path.
controls.threat: Credential interception, adversary-in-the-middle, protocol downgrade (telnet, FTP, SMBv1, NTLMv1, HTTP).
controls.assessment_question: Are only encrypted, authenticated protocols used for administration (SSH, RDP with NLA/TLS, WinRM over HTTPS, HTTPS consoles), with legacy protocols disabled?
evidence_required: scan results showing no cleartext admin protocols
controls.validation_procedure:
Windows: RDP NLA via `(Get-ItemProperty "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server\WinStations\RDP-Tcp").UserAuthentication`; `winrm enumerate winrm/config/listener`; `Get-SmbServerConfiguration | select RequireSecuritySignature,EnableSMB1Protocol`; LmCompatibilityLevel under `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa`.
Linux: `sshd -T | egrep "ciphers|macs|kexalgorithms"` and `ss -tlnp | egrep ":23 |:21 |:80 "`.
Authorised scan: `nmap -sV -p 21,23,80,445,3389,5985,5986 <ip>`.

automation.method: Nmap and credentialed scanner checks; OpenSCAP and CIS-CAT.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Cleartext and legacy protocols in use.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Secure protocols mandated and legacy disabled on most servers.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Enforced by baseline with continuous verification and alerts on cleartext admin traffic.

controls.remediation_guidance: Disable legacy protocols, require NLA/TLS and SSH with modern ciphers, and enforce SMB signing.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 AC-17; Microsoft privileged access (enterprise access model); CIS Controls 4 and 12

controls.name: Servers are administered only from hardened administrative workstations or jump hosts
controls.objective: Keep administrator credentials off general-purpose, internet-exposed workstations.
controls.business_justification: Admin credentials typed on a compromised daily-use machine hand attackers the keys to the servers.
controls.threat: Theft of administrator credentials from compromised workstations.
controls.assessment_question: Are servers administered only from dedicated, hardened workstations or jump hosts that meet endpoint security requirements, with direct administration from standard workstations blocked?
evidence_required: firewall rules allowing admin protocols only from jump hosts
controls.validation_procedure:
Review firewall and host-firewall rules for source restrictions on 22, 3389, 5985 and 5986.
Attempt administrative logon from a standard workstation (expect failure).
Verify the PAW build baseline, no email or browsing, MFA and EDR, and sample session recordings.

automation.method: Firewall rule analysis; PAW compliance via Intune or Defender.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Administration from any workstation.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Jump hosts or PAWs required for administration of critical servers.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Tiered administration with enforced PAWs, session recording and just-in-time access.

controls.remediation_guidance: Introduce a tiered admin model with PAWs or bastions and block admin protocols from other sources.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 AC-17; Microsoft privileged access (enterprise access model); CIS Controls 4 and 12

controls.name: Operationally critical servers are covered by a defined backup scope with RPO and RTO
controls.objective: Ensure critical data, configuration and system state can be recovered to agreed objectives.
controls.business_justification: Unrecoverable data loss or prolonged outage is an existential risk for many organisations, particularly under ransomware.
controls.threat: Permanent data loss and unrecoverable ransomware outage.
controls.assessment_question: Are all servers holding operationally critical data or services included in a documented backup scope with defined recovery point and recovery time objectives?
evidence_required: backup job list versus server inventory
controls.validation_procedure:
Reconcile backup console assets with the server inventory and business-critical list.
Check the last successful backup per server and the follow-up of failures.
Windows: `vssadmin list shadows`, `Get-WBSummary`. Linux: `systemctl list-timers | grep -i backup`.
Confirm system state and configuration are backed up, not just data.

automation.method: Backup platform API reconciled with CMDB; failure alerts to ticketing.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Backups are informal and incomplete.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Documented scope with RPO/RTO and monitored backup jobs.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Scope driven by business impact analysis, with automated coverage assurance.

controls.remediation_guidance: Define RPO/RTO from the business impact analysis, onboard all critical servers, and alert on missed or failed jobs.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-34 Rev.1; 3-2-1-1-0 backup practice; CIS Control 11

controls.name: System, application and data restoration procedures are documented and accessible
controls.objective: Ensure recovery can be executed under pressure by someone other than the original author.
controls.business_justification: Slow or failed recovery extends outage costs; plans stored only on affected systems are unusable.
controls.threat: Delayed or failed recovery during incidents.
controls.assessment_question: Are system, application, configuration and data restoration procedures documented, current, available offline, and aligned to BCP and DR plans?
controls.validation_procedure:
Review runbooks for restoration order, credential escrow, licence keys and dependencies (DNS, AD, certificates).
Confirm copies are accessible without production services (offline or printed).
Ask an engineer to walk through a bare-metal restore of a critical server.

automation.method: Runbook review reminders in the document system.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: No documented recovery procedures.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Documented runbooks reviewed annually and available offline.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Runbooks tested in exercises and updated after every change or test.

controls.remediation_guidance: Write and test runbooks including dependencies, and keep an offline copy.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-34 Rev.1; 3-2-1-1-0 backup practice; CIS Control 11

controls.name: Backups are verified and restores are tested on a defined schedule
controls.objective: Prove that backups are usable and that recovery meets objectives.
controls.business_justification: Untested backups frequently fail when needed; testing converts assumption into assurance.
controls.threat: Silent backup failure or corruption discovered during a crisis.
controls.assessment_question: Are backups integrity-verified and restore-tested at least monthly for critical systems and at least annually for full DR, with results recorded?
evidence_required: DR exercise results with achieved RTO and RPO
controls.validation_procedure:
Select 3 critical servers and obtain the latest restore-test evidence (date, scope, success, time versus RTO).
If none exists, perform a supervised test restore to an isolated network.
Review failures and corrective actions.

automation.method: Backup platform automated recovery verification (for example sandbox restore testing).

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Restores are never tested.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Monthly verification and annual DR test with documented results.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Automated recovery verification with measured RTO/RPO against targets.

controls.remediation_guidance: Schedule monthly verification and annual DR tests, record results, and fix failures.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-34 Rev.1; 3-2-1-1-0 backup practice; CIS Control 11

controls.name: An off-site and offline or immutable backup copy exists
controls.objective: Ensure at least one recovery copy survives site loss and attacker deletion.
controls.business_justification: Ransomware operators target backups first; immutable and offline copies determine whether recovery is possible without paying.
controls.threat: Ransomware encrypting or deleting online backups, and same-site disaster.
controls.assessment_question: Does the backup strategy include at least one off-site copy and one offline or immutable copy protected from deletion by compromised administrator credentials?
controls.validation_procedure:
In a test scope, attempt deletion of a restore point using a production backup-admin account (expect denial).
Cloud checks: `aws s3api get-object-lock-configuration --bucket <bucket>`; Azure immutable storage policy; Veeam hardened repository settings.
Confirm geographic separation of the off-site copy.

automation.method: Cloud storage policy queries; backup platform configuration export.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: All backups are online in the same site.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Off-site copy exists and a separate offline or immutable copy is maintained.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Immutable, geographically separated copies with verified deletion protection and regular tests.

controls.remediation_guidance: Implement immutable or offline copies off-site and require dual authorisation for deletion.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-34 Rev.1; 3-2-1-1-0 backup practice; CIS Control 11

controls.name: Backups are encrypted in transit and at rest and media is handled securely
controls.objective: Protect confidentiality of backup data wherever it is stored or transmitted.
controls.business_justification: Backups contain the full data set; their compromise is equivalent to a breach of the source systems.
controls.threat: Theft or exposure of backup copies and interception in transit.
controls.assessment_question: Are backups encrypted in transit and at rest, with keys managed separately from the backup data, and is backup media handled per a media security standard?
controls.validation_procedure:
Inspect job settings for encryption and TLS.
Confirm key escrow is separate from the backup server.
Sample tape or media chain-of-custody records.
Confirm via capture or scan that backup traffic is encrypted.

automation.method: Backup platform configuration export; network protocol scan.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Backups are unencrypted and media handling is informal.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Encryption enabled with documented key management and media standard.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: End-to-end encryption with HSM or KMS-managed keys and audited media handling.

controls.remediation_guidance: Enable backup encryption, separate key management, and adopt a media handling standard.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-34 Rev.1; 3-2-1-1-0 backup practice; CIS Control 11

controls.name: Backup infrastructure and credentials are segregated from production administration
controls.objective: Prevent a single compromised administrator or domain from destroying both production and backups.
controls.business_justification: Backup systems joined to the production domain are routinely compromised and wiped in ransomware attacks.
controls.threat: Compromised domain administrator deleting production data and backups.
controls.assessment_question: Are backup servers, consoles and credentials separated from production administration through separate identities, MFA, network isolation and restricted console access?
controls.validation_procedure:
Windows: `(Get-CimInstance Win32_ComputerSystem).PartOfDomain` to determine whether the backup server is domain-joined.
Review membership of backup administrator groups and MFA on the console.
Check that deletion and retention-change actions are audited and alerted.

automation.method: Backup platform audit log export; AD group membership reports.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Backup servers are domain-joined and managed by domain administrators.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Dedicated backup administrators with MFA and restricted network access.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Isolated backup domain or workgroup, dual authorisation for destructive actions and alerts.

controls.remediation_guidance: Separate backup identities and network from production, require MFA, and alert on destructive actions.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-34 Rev.1; 3-2-1-1-0 backup practice; CIS Control 11

controls.name: Sensitive data on servers is encrypted at rest
controls.objective: Protect data on disks, volumes and databases from exposure through theft or improper access to storage.
controls.business_justification: Encryption at rest limits the impact of lost drives, snapshots and storage-level access.
controls.threat: Data exposure from stolen disks, backups and snapshots.
controls.assessment_question: Is sensitive data encrypted at rest through full-disk, volume or database encryption, with keys protected and recoverable?
controls.validation_procedure:
Windows: `manage-bde -status` and `Get-BitLockerVolume`.
Linux: `lsblk -f` (look for crypto_LUKS) and `cryptsetup status <name>`.
SQL Server: `SELECT name,is_encrypted FROM sys.databases`.
Verify recovery key escrow and who can retrieve keys.

automation.method: BitLocker reports through Intune or MBAM; configuration management queries.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: No encryption at rest.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Encryption on servers holding sensitive data with escrowed keys.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Encryption everywhere with managed rotation and monitoring of key access.

controls.remediation_guidance: Enable disk and database encryption, escrow recovery keys, and restrict retrieval.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-111; NIST SP 800-52 Rev.2; CIS Control 3

controls.name: Server services use current TLS versions, strong ciphers and managed certificates
controls.objective: Ensure encrypted channels are actually strong and certificates are valid and managed.
controls.business_justification: Weak protocols enable decryption and downgrade; expired certificates cause outages.
