controls.threat: Downgrade and adversary-in-the-middle attacks, weak cipher decryption, expired certificates.
controls.assessment_question: Do services use TLS 1.2 or higher with strong cipher suites and valid, managed certificates, with SSLv3 and TLS 1.0/1.1 disabled?
controls.validation_procedure:
`nmap --script ssl-enum-ciphers -p 443,636,3389 <ip>` or `testssl.sh <host>:443`.
Windows: `Get-TlsCipherSuite` and the SCHANNEL registry keys under `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL\Protocols`.
Linux: `openssl ciphers -v`; certificate expiry via `openssl s_client -connect <host>:443 | openssl x509 -noout -dates`.

automation.method: testssl.sh or SSL Labs-style scanning; certificate lifecycle management tools.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Legacy protocols and unmanaged certificates.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Cryptographic standard enforced on most services with certificate inventory.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Automated crypto compliance scanning and certificate renewal.

controls.remediation_guidance: Disable legacy protocols and weak ciphers, inventory certificates, and automate renewal.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-111; NIST SP 800-52 Rev.2; CIS Control 3

controls.name: File systems enforce access control and permissions on sensitive data
controls.objective: Ensure storage uses file systems capable of enforcing permissions and that permissions are appropriate.
controls.business_justification: Without enforceable permissions, any local or network user can read or alter sensitive data.
controls.threat: Unauthorised data access or modification on file systems without permission enforcement.
controls.assessment_question: Are non-removable media formatted with access-control-capable file systems (NTFS, ReFS, ext4/XFS with ACLs), with appropriate permissions and no FAT file systems for sensitive volumes?
controls.validation_procedure:
Windows: `Get-Volume | select DriveLetter,FileSystem` and `icacls D:\Data`.
Linux: `lsblk -f`, `mount | grep -E "vfat|ntfs-3g"`, `getfacl -R /srv/data | head`, and `findmnt` to check nodev, nosuid and noexec options where appropriate.

automation.method: Configuration management file system and ACL reports.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Sensitive data on file systems without permission support.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Access-control file systems with documented permission standards.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Permissions baselined and monitored with automated drift detection.

controls.remediation_guidance: Migrate sensitive volumes to ACL-capable file systems and apply least-privilege permissions.
controls.references: NIST SP 800-111; NIST SP 800-52 Rev.2; CIS Control 3

controls.name: Every server is registered in an authoritative inventory reconciled with discovery
controls.objective: Maintain an accurate record of all servers, their role, owner and lifecycle.
controls.business_justification: Unknown servers are unpatched, unmonitored and unowned, and are favoured footholds for attackers.
controls.threat: Shadow or forgotten servers.
controls.assessment_question: Is every server registered in an authoritative inventory or CMDB (owner, role, OS, criticality, location, network address, lifecycle), and is it reconciled with network discovery?
controls.validation_procedure:
Obtain discovery data (`nmap -sn <subnets>`, DHCP, DNS and ARP exports, hypervisor inventory, cloud APIs) and compare it with the CMDB.
Quantify unmatched hosts in both directions and check mandatory fields for completeness.

automation.method: Scheduled discovery reconciled with CMDB via API.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: No reliable server inventory.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Maintained CMDB with a registration step in provisioning.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Automated discovery and reconciliation with exceptions closed within defined time.

controls.remediation_guidance: Make registration part of provisioning and reconcile discovery with the CMDB at least monthly.
controls.references: ISO/IEC 27005; NIST SP 800-30 Rev.1; NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 RA and SA families; ISO/IEC 27036 (supplier relationships)

controls.name: Every server has accountable owners, a criticality rating and a data classification
controls.objective: Ensure clear accountability and risk-based treatment of each server.
controls.business_justification: Unclear ownership delays response and leaves patching, backup and monitoring unprioritised.
controls.threat: Unmanaged systems and misprioritised protection.
controls.assessment_question: Does every server have a named business owner, system administrator and application administrator approved by management, with criticality and data classification recorded and responsibilities for server-standard compliance documented?
controls.validation_procedure:
Sample 10 servers and verify named owners and administrators are current employees and approved.
Confirm criticality and classification drive patching, backup and monitoring tiers.
Verify application administrators are accountable for application-level compliance with the server standard.

automation.method: CMDB mandatory fields; HR-to-CMDB owner validation.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Ownership is unknown or informal.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Named owners and administrators recorded with criticality.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Automated owner validation and risk-based service tiers driving controls.

controls.remediation_guidance: Make owner, administrators, criticality and classification mandatory CMDB fields with periodic validation.
controls.references: ISO/IEC 27005; NIST SP 800-30 Rev.1; NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 RA and SA families; ISO/IEC 27036 (supplier relationships)

controls.name: A security review and risk assessment is completed before production and on significant change
controls.objective: Ensure risk is understood and formally accepted before a server enters service.
controls.business_justification: Risk assessed after go-live is difficult to remediate and leaves leadership accepting unknown exposure.
controls.threat: Unassessed systems deployed with unmanaged risk.
controls.assessment_question: Is a security review and risk assessment completed for new servers and significant changes before production by an approved assessor, with residual risk accepted by the owner?
controls.validation_procedure:
Sample 5 new servers and verify the risk assessment date precedes go-live, the assessor, findings and the owner's risk acceptance.
Confirm re-assessment triggers and scheduled review dates exist.

automation.method: Workflow gate in provisioning requiring an attached assessment ID.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: No pre-production risk assessment.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Standard assessment completed with owner acceptance for new servers.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Threat-informed assessments integrated into provisioning with periodic reassessment.

controls.remediation_guidance: Introduce a mandatory pre-production risk assessment and risk acceptance step, and reassess on change.
controls.references: ISO/IEC 27005; NIST SP 800-30 Rev.1; NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 RA and SA families; ISO/IEC 27036 (supplier relationships)

controls.name: Third-party system administration and hosting are governed through contracts and access controls
controls.objective: Manage risk introduced by vendors who administer, host or support servers.
controls.business_justification: Third parties with privileged access are a leading supply-chain breach vector.
controls.threat: Third-party compromise and unmanaged vendor access.
controls.assessment_question: Are contracts for outsourced administration, hosting and support reviewed for security and risk clauses (access, audit rights, breach notification, subcontractors), and is third-party access controlled?
controls.validation_procedure:
Sample 3 contracts for required clauses.
Review vendor accounts and remote access methods (MFA, session recording, time-bound access).
Obtain assurance reports and map complementary user entity controls to internal controls.

automation.method: Vendor access reports from PAM; vendor risk platform integration.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Vendors have standing access with no security terms.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Contracts include security clauses and vendor access is controlled.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Continuous vendor monitoring, just-in-time recorded access, and annual assurance review.

controls.remediation_guidance: Add security clauses and audit rights, enforce MFA and recorded just-in-time vendor access, and review assurance reports.
controls.references: ISO/IEC 27005; NIST SP 800-30 Rev.1; NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 RA and SA families; ISO/IEC 27036 (supplier relationships)

controls.name: Virtualization management planes are isolated and hardened
controls.objective: Protect the interfaces that control all hosted workloads.
controls.business_justification: Compromise of vCenter, an ESXi host or a Hyper-V or Proxmox management interface gives control of every VM and datastore.
controls.threat: Management-plane exploitation, including ESXi and vCenter ransomware campaigns.
controls.assessment_question: Are hypervisor and management interfaces (vCenter, ESXi, Hyper-V Manager/SCVMM/WAC, Proxmox GUI/API) restricted to a management network, not internet-exposed, and secured with TLS and trusted certificates?
controls.validation_procedure:
Scan public ranges for 443, 902, 8006, 5985 and 22 and compare with documented exposure.
From a user VLAN test reachability of management addresses.
VMware: `Get-VMHost | Get-VMHostFirewallException | where Enabled`. Proxmox: `pve-firewall status` and `ss -tlnp | grep -E "8006|22"`. Hyper-V: `Get-NetFirewallRule -DisplayGroup "Hyper-V*" -Enabled True`.

automation.method: External attack-surface scans; PowerCLI and PowerShell configuration reports.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Management interfaces reachable from the user network or internet.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Dedicated management network with firewall restrictions.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Management plane behind jump hosts with MFA, continuous exposure monitoring and CA-issued certificates.

controls.remediation_guidance: Isolate management interfaces on a restricted network and remove any internet exposure.
controls.references: VMware vSphere Security Configuration Guide; Microsoft Hyper-V security documentation; CIS Benchmarks (VMware ESXi); Proxmox VE administration guide; NIST SP 800-125

controls.name: Hypervisor administrative access uses central identity, MFA and least privilege
controls.objective: Prevent unmanaged or shared privileged access to the virtualization layer.
controls.business_justification: Local root accounts on hosts bypass SSO and MFA and are rarely monitored.
controls.threat: Shared root credentials and bypass of central identity.
controls.assessment_question: Is hypervisor and management access integrated with central identity, protected by MFA, role-based with least privilege, with local root or administrator accounts vaulted and lockdown mode or equivalent enforced?
evidence_required: vCenter SSO and identity source configuration
controls.validation_procedure:
VMware: `Get-VMHost | select Name,@{N='Lockdown';E={$_.ExtensionData.Config.LockdownMode}}` and `Get-VIPermission | select Principal,Role,Entity`.
Hyper-V: `Get-LocalGroupMember "Hyper-V Administrators"`.
Proxmox: `pveum user list`, `pveum acl list`, and GUI Datacenter > Permissions > Two Factor.
Confirm the break-glass local account is vaulted and alerted.

automation.method: PowerCLI permission export; Proxmox API user and ACL export.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: Shared root credentials used directly on hosts.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Central identity with role-based access and vaulted local accounts.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: MFA, lockdown mode and just-in-time access with alerting on any local account use.

controls.remediation_guidance: Integrate with central identity, enable lockdown mode, enforce MFA and vault local accounts.
controls.references: VMware vSphere Security Configuration Guide; Microsoft Hyper-V security documentation; CIS Benchmarks (VMware ESXi); Proxmox VE administration guide; NIST SP 800-125

controls.name: Virtual machines are built from hardened templates with controlled snapshots and devices
controls.objective: Reduce guest attack surface and data exposure through VM configuration.
controls.business_justification: Forgotten snapshots, attached media and unmanaged VMs create hidden data exposure and escape surfaces.
controls.threat: VM escape, snapshot data exposure, rogue or unmanaged VMs.
controls.assessment_question: Are VMs built from hardened templates with unnecessary virtual hardware removed, snapshots and checkpoints controlled, guest tools patched and VM escape surfaces minimised?
controls.validation_procedure:
VMware: `Get-VM | Get-Snapshot | select VM,Name,Created`, `Get-VM | Get-CDDrive | where {$_.IsoPath}`, and check isolation.tools settings against the VMware Security Configuration Guide.
Hyper-V: `Get-VMSnapshot -VMName *`, `Get-VMFirmware -VMName * | select VMName,SecureBoot`.
Proxmox: `qm list` and `qm config <vmid>` for unused USB, serial or CD devices.

automation.method: PowerCLI and PowerShell hardening audits.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: VMs created ad hoc from arbitrary media.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Hardened templates with snapshot lifecycle limits.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Templates versioned as code with automated compliance and snapshot expiry.

controls.remediation_guidance: Standardise hardened VM templates, delete stale snapshots, and remove unused virtual devices.
controls.references: VMware vSphere Security Configuration Guide; Microsoft Hyper-V security documentation; CIS Benchmarks (VMware ESXi); Proxmox VE administration guide; NIST SP 800-125

controls.name: Virtual networks and storage access are segmented and restricted
controls.objective: Prevent cross-VM and cross-zone access through virtual switching and storage networks.
controls.business_justification: Flat virtual networks and open storage exports allow lateral movement and data theft below the guest OS.
controls.threat: Sniffing, lateral movement across VMs, unauthorised storage mounts.
controls.assessment_question: Are virtual switches, VLANs, storage networks (vMotion, iSCSI, NFS, replication) and management traffic segregated, with promiscuous mode, MAC changes and forged transmits restricted, and storage access controlled?
evidence_required: virtual firewall rules (NSX, Hyper-V extended ACLs, Proxmox SDN)
controls.validation_procedure:
VMware: `Get-VirtualSwitch | Get-SecurityPolicy` and `Get-VirtualPortGroup | Get-SecurityPolicy` (AllowPromiscuous, MacChanges and ForgedTransmits should be Reject); confirm vMotion uses a dedicated VLAN.
Hyper-V: `Get-VMNetworkAdapter * | select VMName,SwitchName,MacAddressSpoofing`.
Proxmox: review `/etc/network/interfaces` and datacenter firewall rules.
Verify iSCSI CHAP and NFS export restrictions.

automation.method: PowerCLI network policy exports; storage array configuration export.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: A single flat virtual network for all traffic.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Separate VLANs for management, storage and workloads with secure switch policies.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Micro-segmentation with distributed firewalling and monitored policy changes.

controls.remediation_guidance: Separate management, storage and workload networks, set secure vSwitch policies, and restrict storage exports.
controls.references: VMware vSphere Security Configuration Guide; Microsoft Hyper-V security documentation; CIS Benchmarks (VMware ESXi); Proxmox VE administration guide; NIST SP 800-125

controls.name: Hypervisor logging and ransomware resilience controls are in place
controls.objective: Detect hypervisor tampering and reduce the impact of hypervisor-targeting ransomware.
controls.business_justification: Attackers encrypt datastores directly from the hypervisor, bypassing guest-level protections.
controls.threat: Hypervisor-targeting ransomware and undetected host tampering.
controls.assessment_question: Are hypervisor and management logs forwarded to the SIEM, shell and SSH services disabled by default, host configuration backed up, and ransomware protections (acceptance levels, execution restrictions, datastore snapshots and backups) in place?
controls.validation_procedure:
VMware: `Get-VMHost | Get-VMHostSysLogServer`; `Get-VMHost | Get-VMHostService | where {$_.Key -in 'TSM','TSM-SSH'} | select VMHost,Key,Running`; `esxcli software acceptance get`; `Get-AdvancedSetting -Entity (Get-VMHost) -Name UserVars.ESXiShellTimeOut`; host configuration backup with `vim-cmd hostsvc/firmware/backup_config`.
Hyper-V: confirm forwarding of Microsoft-Windows-Hyper-V-* event logs.
Proxmox: `journalctl -u pveproxy`, rsyslog forwarding and Proxmox Backup Server jobs.

automation.method: PowerCLI compliance scripts; SIEM source monitoring.

maturity_anchors.l1_initial: No hypervisor logging; SSH left enabled.
maturity_anchors.l3_defined: Logs forwarded, SSH disabled by default, host configuration backed up.
maturity_anchors.l5_optimized: Detection use cases for hypervisor attacks, immutable datastore backups and tested recovery.

controls.remediation_guidance: Forward hypervisor logs, disable SSH and shell by default, back up host configuration, and test datastore recovery.
controls.references: VMware vSphere Security Configuration Guide; Microsoft Hyper-V security documentation; CIS Benchmarks (VMware ESXi); Proxmox VE administration guide; NIST SP 800-125
